CORRECTIONS REQUIRED
An audit of the extractions against Mireia Ryšková’s article, "The Reception of the Book of Isaiah in Paul’s Letter to the Romans" (2019), confirms that all extracted claims, page locators, and verbatim quotations are grounded in the text, but identifies three technical adjustments needed to preserve the author's exact qualifications, scholarly attributions, and disjunctive framing.
Itemized Audit Findings & Corrections
1. Qualification on the Origin of the Composite Stone Citation in Romans 9:33 (Check #4, #5, & #6)
Location: Page 103 (Section 5: Rom 9:33).
Previous Extraction: Stated as a settled fact (S06F-E004) that Paul personally merged Isaiah 28:16 and Isaiah 8:14 into a composite quotation.
Source Observation: On page 103, Ryšková explicitly presents the origin of the composite text as an unresolved scholarly debate: "Some scholars (Koch and Dodd, for example) believe that the combination is a pre-Pauline tradition (Koch oral; Dodd written) and that Paul is therefore quoting from Isaiah on the basis of an existing text... Shum is certain that Paul is quoting directly from a scroll of Isaiah he might have had access to in Corinth" [p. 103, fn. 35–36].
Correction: Refine claim S06F-E004 to state that while Ryšková identifies Rom 9:33 as a composite of Isaiah 28:16 and 8:14, she explicitly presents it as an open question whether Paul inherited a pre-Pauline oral/written testimonia tradition (Koch/Dodd) or compiled the texts directly from an Isaiah scroll (Shum).
2. Preservation of Disjunctive Possibilities in Rom 11:34 / Isaiah 40:13 (Check #4 & #6)
Location: Page 108 (Section 12: Rom 11:34–35).
Previous Extraction: Converted Ryšková's disjunctive explanation into a single definitive claim regarding Paul's quotation method, and treated Job 41:11 as a definite quotation.
Source Observation: On page 108, Ryšková uses explicitly qualified disjunctive language: Paul is "either quoting by heart from his great knowledge of Isaiah or using Isaiah’s language automatically, naturally", and describes the link in Rom 11:35 to Job 41:11 (LXX 41:3) as a "possible echo", not a settled citation [p. 108].
Correction: Refine claim S06F-E006 to reflect that Ryšková offers two alternative explanations for Paul's unannounced quotation of Isaiah 40:13 (quoting from memory vs. automatic reliance on biblical idiom) and qualifies the accompanying Job 41:11 allusion as a "possible echo".
3. Explicit Attribution to Shum for Christological Co-Sovereignty (Check #5)
Location: Page 104 (Section 6: Rom 10:11).
Previous Extraction: Attributed the formulation that Christ is "co-sovereign and co-unique with God the Father" (S06F-E003) directly to Ryšková without noting her footnote source.
Source Observation: On page 104, Ryšková makes this statement while citing Shiu-Lun Shum (Paul's Use of Isaiah in Romans, p. 223) in footnote 40 [p. 104, fn. 40].
Correction: Note in claim S06F-E003 that Ryšková's characterization of Christ as "co-sovereign and co-unique with God the Father" in Isaiah's monotheistic statements relies directly on Shiu-Lun Shum's monograph [p. 104, fn. 40].
Audit Verification Across the 7 Audit Checks
Direct Source Support (Check #1): Verified. All extracted claims for Rom 9:33, Rom 10:11, Rom 10:13, Rom 11:34, and Rom 15:12 correspond directly to Ryšková's exposition.
Quotation Accuracy (Check #2): Verified. All short exact quotations match the printed text of AUC Theologica 9/2 (2019) without material omissions.
Observed Printed Page Numbers (Check #3): Verified. All locators were observed directly from the page footers/headers of ryskova_2019_isaiah_romans.pdf (pages 95–116).
Possibility vs. Certainty (Check #4): Addressed in Items 1 and 2 above.
Scholar Attribution (Check #5): Addressed in Items 1 and 3 above.
Qualifications and Textual Variants (Check #6): Addressed in Items 1 and 2 above.
No General Model Knowledge (Check #7): Verified. No external model knowledge was introduced into the audit or extractions.
💡 Next Steps:
Would you like a master comparative report cross-referencing all audited extractions across the five project sources (Sanday & Headlam 1895, Robertson & Plummer 1914, Lightfoot 1865/1914, Wilk 1998, and Ryšková 2019)?
I can also compile a structured summary report artifact in your Studio panel.
